purpose: Native evidence for the five wave facts this package owns: forge.trigger.objective.{wave_started,wave_spawned,wave_exhausted,wave_cleared,spawn_shortfall}. Every fact is a Forge derivation, because the game has no wave event for any of them.
gameVerifiedNote: Not one of these hooks has been observed in a running game. Every signature, RVA and field name below is read from the build 20403457 interop assemblies and from the frozen hook analysis in ForgeMap/evidence/encounter-wave-hooks.json; the derivations are Forge's, and the in-game checks listed at the end have not been run.
sourceEvidence: interop dump of Modules-ASM.dll: SurvivalWave (fields m_settings, m_state, m_waveSpawnTimer, m_groupSpawnTimer, m_populationPointsSpentTotal, m_populationPointsSpentDuringWave, m_populationPointsPerWaveMax, m_isNewWave), Mastermind (Current, m_activeGroups, m_nextEventID, MastermindEvent.EventID), Enemies.EnemyGroup (Members, SurvivalWave, m_waveID, GroupType, Data)
ForgeEnemy/evidence/enemy-behavior-hooks.json (the enemy module's own hook and thread discipline)

hooks.patch: prefix captures the native instance, postfix publishes
hooks.whyPostfix: The wave's own identity is Mastermind.MastermindEvent.EventID, and OnSpawn is the body that registers the event with Mastermind.AddEvent (encounter-wave-hooks.json hooks[0] and hooks[9]). Reading the id in the prefix would either read zero or read a value the spawn body is about to assign, so the fact is published after the body ran and an id of zero publishes nothing.
hooks.side: both (replicator spawn callback); the observation is gated to the master by the module's own CanExecute, and a publish from a non-host world is refused by the kernel with not-host

hooks.patch: SpawnGroup prefix opens the batch and its postfix closes it; RegisterGroup postfix adds one delivered group
hooks.side: host (the wave state machine is the master's: encounter-wave-hooks.json hooks[4] and hooks[7])

hooks.patch: RegisterCost postfix counts a payment inside the open batch; RegisterGroup postfix counts a delivery; SpawnGroup postfix compares the two

hooks.why: There is no wave-exhausted event (waveStateWithoutNativeEvent[0]). TryEndEvent is the wave's own completion test, and it is the closest native signal to 'nothing left to spend' that the frozen analysis found (encounter-wave-hooks.json hooks[5]).

Cleared has to be derived (waveStateWithoutNativeEvent[0]); the group list after the Mastermind's own maintenance is the native answer to 'is anything of this wave still alive' (encounter-wave-hooks.json hooks[15]). Mastermind.UnregisterGroup (0x14F8960, hooks[13]) is the other candidate point, and it was not used: an event-driven check can only be as complete as the set of removal paths that call it, while the post-maintenance list cannot miss one.

hooks.patch: prefix retires the wave's entry in this provider's table
hooks.why: The callback fires for every teardown, level cleanup and event cancellation included (encounter-wave-hooks.json hooks[1]). Publishing cleaned or stopped from it would report a cancelled encounter as a won one, so it publishes nothing.

reads.note: The runtime wave instance identity, and the one the rulings name (a wave is identified by the Mastermind event id). SurvivalWave derives from Mastermind.MastermindEvent, so every hook reads it from the instance it already has.
singleton; null before the world has a Mastermind, in which case the cleared check publishes nothing rather than guessing
membership is tested by native pointer, never by managed wrapper identity
the batch's members; a member this provider has no live life for is left out of the frame
the key this provider's own life table uses; a member is published only when the tracked instance is the same wrapper and the reference still resolves

derivations.formula: SurvivalWave.OnSpawn completed AND wave.EventID != 0 AND the instance is not already in this world's table

one SurvivalWave.SpawnGroup call: spawned = the distinct EnemyGroup.Members of every group SurvivalWave.RegisterGroup delivered inside that call, filtered to the members this provider still has a live life for; count = that number
derivations.source: SpawnGroup (batch boundary), RegisterGroup (delivery), EnemyGroup.Members (native member list)
derivations.batchBoundary: The game has no batch event. A batch is defined as one SurvivalWave.SpawnGroup call, which is the per-group spawn step the frozen analysis names as the point wave_spawned should be derived from (encounter-wave-hooks.json hooks[4]). A group registered outside such a call belongs to no batch and is only counted in the wave's own group total.

derivations.formula: inside one batch: requested = the number of SurvivalWave.RegisterCost calls, spawned = the number of distinct groups SurvivalWave.RegisterGroup delivered; the fact fires only when requested > spawned
derivations.source: RegisterCost (the wave paying for a group), RegisterGroup (the group it produced)
derivations.note: The frame carries no reason port, so none is published. The comparison is between the groups the wave paid for and the groups it produced, which is the requested-versus-delivered reading the frozen analysis names; a population-point comparison is not made, because the two fields' exact semantics are field names only (unproven[2] of the source evidence).

derivations.formula: SurvivalWave.TryEndEvent() returned true; count = the groups this wave registered over its whole life
derivations.source: TryEndEvent (native completion test), RegisterGroup (native group count)
derivations.note: One fact per wave instance. TryEndEvent answering false is not a fact.

derivations.formula: after Mastermind.MaintainGroups: the wave has registered at least one group and none of its groups is in Mastermind.m_activeGroups
derivations.source: MaintainGroups (native maintenance), m_activeGroups (native live list), RegisterGroup (which groups are this wave's)
derivations.note: A wave that never registered a group is not cleared, and a wave whose teardown was observed is gone before this check can run.

ports.declared: handle, handleKind effect, lifetime encounter, optional
ports.why: This runtime mints no handle for a provider: the kernel's handle pool is created by RuntimeKernel.CreateHandle (RuntimeKernel.Handles.cs:48) and is private to the kernel, whose only provider-facing uses are the schedule and lease APIs. The catalog declares the wave instance as a handle output, and a required port the provider cannot fill would make every publish fail the kernel's own event shape check; the always-null form is refused by the ruling that allows an absent value. The port is therefore optional and absent, and the wave's runtime identity travels in the event frame's scope id, gtfo.wave:<worldEpoch>:<EventID> — the same identity discipline the attack facts use. A plan cannot even wire the port: the kernel refuses to wire an optional event port at load (optional-event-port), so the absence is loud rather than silent.
ports.reshapeProposal: Either land provider-owned handle minting and declare the port required again, or drop the port from the website row and keep the scope id as the instance identity.

ports.published: yes, from the native values above
declaration only (a compile-time author reference, matched against the plan's mount)
ports.blocker: The kernel's ParameterTypes table (RuntimeGraphContracts.cs:388) does not carry resource, while the website's graphParameterTypes does, so a row that spells this parameter is refused at registration with parameter-type. The five rows keep the catalog's spelling; the kernel table has to gain the member (ruling 49's structural resource parameter) in the R-ABI batch.

rowDeltas.reason: see ports[0]; a required port that can never be filled makes all five rows dead

The catalog's own targetOwner for these rows is Enemy, and the plan-load domain check refuses a plan whose domain is not one of its nodes' domains; the attack rows of this same package already spell enemy. Proposed catalog alignment, not a port or parameter change.

unproven: Mastermind.AddEvent is the only caller of OnSpawn's registration path in the frozen analysis, but whether EventID is assigned inside OnSpawn (making the postfix read the authoritative value) or carried in from pSurvivalWaveSpawnData was not decoded. The implementation reads the instance's own EventID after the body and publishes nothing when it is zero.

EnemyGroup.Members is read when the SpawnGroup call returns; whether the members are all populated at that instant, or some are added as the group's spawn coroutine runs, was not established. A batch therefore reports the members that exist when its own native call returns, and never more.

SurvivalWave.RegisterGroup's isRecall flag was not decoded. The implementation counts every registration, deduplicated by native group pointer, so a recall of a group already counted is not a second delivery; requested-versus-delivered stays a group-count comparison.
wave_exhausted's count is this provider's own tally of RegisterGroup calls for the wave; the game exposes no per-wave group list, so the tally is Forge's, not the game's.
Every side and host claim above is inference from the call graph and the Master naming; the Mastermind singleton was not observed at runtime (unproven[0] of the source evidence).

The kernel refuses an optional event port at plan load (optional-event-port), which is why no plan can wire the wave port; that behaviour was observed in this slice's own test project rather than inferred.
inGameVerificationPlan: Spawn a survival wave and confirm wave_started fires once with the EventID the Mastermind assigned, and that the scope id matches it.
Confirm a wave's SpawnGroup call registers exactly the groups RegisterGroup reports for that call, so count matches the enemies the game actually placed.
Force a spawn shortfall (a wave whose population budget cannot place a group) and confirm requested exceeds spawned in the same batch.
Confirm wave_exhausted fires once when the wave's own TryEndEvent answers true, and not on a wave that is merely paused.
Kill a wave's enemies and confirm wave_cleared fires once, after the Mastermind's group list drops the last group, and not on level cleanup or objective cancellation.
Confirm a wave hook with no subscribing plan reads no game state (the family's own subscriber gate).
